title: An unset optional field is omitted from the body, not sent as null
why: The server's decoder rejects a null even where the field is optional, and each language defaults differently: Python serialises None as null, JavaScript keeps an explicit null, Go omits a nil pointer. Without this case the three SDKs would send three different bodies and two of them would get 400 INVALID_INPUT for a call the author wrote correctly. The headers pin the OTHER half: exactly one credential leaves the client. The server answers 401 to a request carrying a developer key next to a session rather than choosing between them, so an SDK that helpfully attached both would turn a valid key into an anonymous rejection — and `Authorization: $absent` is the half that catches it, because a case that only checked the key present would pass either way.
